wire_delta.conclusion: Two wire blocks differ between draft 21 and draft 22. LOCATION_FILTER Parameter is a real wire change (#1913, #1953): the draft 21 length-prefixed form (Parameter Type, Length (vi64), optional StartGroup, StartObject, EndGroupDelta, EndObject, with the field count inferred from Length) is replaced by Parameter Type followed by an explicit Location Filter Type (vi64) in place of the Length field, which selects the fields that follow: 0x00 no filter, 0x01 relative StartGroup, 0x02 StartGroup and StartObject, 0x03 adds EndGroupDelta, 0x04 adds EndObject, 0x05 Next Object with no fields; any other Location Filter Type is a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION, so encoders and decoders of 0x21 (top level and inside FILL_PARAMETERS) must change and sub-project B (the codec task) must cover it. PUBLISH_NAMESPACE Message is editorial: its field Track Namespace (..) is renamed Track Namespace Prefix (..) with the same Section 8.7 Track Namespace encoding and position, prefix matching was already the draft 21 behavior (Section 7.5 of draft 21), and the new statement that AUTHORIZATION_TOKEN is the only allowed parameter matches draft 21 Section 9.20.3, so the bytes on the wire are unchanged and no codec change is needed for it. No blocks were added or removed. The Next Object encoding also changed: draft 21 used StartGroup=0, StartObject=0 under the length-inferred form, while draft 22 uses Location Filter Type 0x05 and Type 0x02 with {0, 0} is now an absolute start.

for_wire_codecs_B: LOCATION_FILTER (Parameter Type 0x21): Location Filter Type (vi64) replaces the draft 21 Length field; 0x00 no filter, 0x01 relative StartGroup, 0x02 StartGroup and StartObject, 0x03 adds EndGroupDelta, 0x04 adds EndObject, 0x05 Next Object with no fields, and any other type is a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (draft 22 lines 5291-5311). The same encoding applies at top level and inside FILL_PARAMETERS.
Next Object is no longer encoded as StartGroup=0, StartObject=0: Type 0x02 with {0, 0} is an absolute start, so the draft 21 two-zero form must map to Type 0x05, not to 0x02.
PUBLISH_NAMESPACE Message: the field Track Namespace is renamed Track Namespace Prefix; the encoding and field position are unchanged.

In l06-announce-prefix the runner opens Announce Streams with an ANNOUNCE_REQUEST for the empty prefix, for a prefix of the publisher's configured broadcast path (both open at once, so two overlapping requests are exercised) and for a prefix disjoint from it, and decodes every message on the response side with the L1b codecs for a stated window (seconds, recorded in the evidence).

The runner sends a well-formed ANNOUNCE_REQUEST whose Message Length covers the prefix plus trailing bytes and judges that the publisher closes the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (session code 0x3); the same session-close evidence carries the code-space check of L06-4-4-MUST-027.
A distinct stimulus: the runner cancels one of two live subscriptions with RESET_STREAM and STOP_SENDING carrying a reserved code (32 through 47).
The publisher receives codes when the runner cancels: the runner ends one of two live subscriptions with RESET_STREAM and STOP_SENDING carrying an unregistered application code (64 or above).
After the setup exchange the runner opens a bidirectional stream with an unregistered STREAM_TYPE and writes nothing else; the publisher must reset it.

The publisher is the peer when the runner ends a transaction: the runner opens an ANNOUNCE_REQUEST and a SUBSCRIBE stream, then closes its send direction with FIN, and observes that the publisher closes its own send direction (FIN or RESET_STREAM).

In l06-setup-client-path the runner (through the adapter) gives the publisher a session URL with a non-empty path and a harmless query component (both recorded in the evidence); L1d runs the scenario on both bindings.

A named deliberate violation probe: the runner's SETUP carries the Cost parameter (0x4, which the runner may legally send once) twice with the same value, so the repetition is the only defect, and the runner sends nothing else that could provoke a close.

A named deliberate violation probe: after its first Setup Stream has been sent and finished, the runner opens a second unidirectional Setup Stream (STREAM_TYPE 0x1, an empty SETUP, FIN), which breaks "exactly one Setup Stream per direction", and sends nothing else.
On binding 1 the runner's SETUP carries a Path parameter, which only the client may send; the publisher must close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (session code 0x3).

The publisher is the client, so this is testable with a named deliberate violation probe: the runner's SETUP carries a Role parameter (value 0, Both, so only the sender is wrong) and nothing else that could provoke a close.

The publisher's half is observable on every session: after accepting the connection the runner records the publisher's unidirectional streams and checks that one carries the Setup STREAM_TYPE, decodes as exactly one SETUP (L1b codec, empty parameter list allowed) and ends with FIN rather than a reset or further bytes.
The runner's SETUP carries one parameter with an id the draft does not define; the publisher must ignore it, so its own SETUP, the ANNOUNCE_OK and an open session are expected.

Observable from the GROUP headers of the publisher's Group streams, using the draft's abutting pattern (Section 3.6): the runner first subscribes with Group Start = G, Group End = G and Frame End = N-1 and receives frames 0 through N-1 of Group G, then subscribes with Group Start = G and Frame Start = N, so the non-zero Frame Start names a Group the runner has received, as the draft requires.

In l06-subscribe-group-floor the runner first learns the latest Group Sequence L from a default subscription in the same session, then opens two floored subscriptions with new Subscribe IDs: Group Start F = L and F = L + 2 (a floor above the latest group, which simply waits), Frame Start 0, Group End 0, and a large Subscriber Max Age; the values are recorded.

The runner sends a SUBSCRIBE with Group End = 0 and a non-zero Frame End (the only violation a publisher can detect from the message alone, since it cannot know which Groups the subscriber has received).

The runner announces, then subscribes to an announced track with a default SUBSCRIBE (latest group, unbounded) and observes Group streams for a stated window long enough to see at least two groups of the target's group cadence (recorded in the evidence; the same window serves L06-6-3-2-MUST-NOT-097).

After an announce exchange the runner opens two Subscribe Streams, each with a conforming SUBSCRIBE: (a) a broadcast path that no route the publisher announced covers (outside every announced prefix), which the publisher cannot serve, and (b) a track name the announced broadcast does not serve.
